parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the difference in reactivity between ethanoyl chloride and chlorobenzene with water.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The structure of compound **V** is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text: Name all the functional groups in **V**.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the number of possible optical isomers for **V**.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest **one** reason, other than better biological activity and lower dosage required, why it is beneficial to synthesise a single optical isomer of **V** for use as a drug.

parts.label: (c)
(d)(i)
parts.stem:
A polypeptide formed from four amino acids, **A**, **B**, **C** and **D**, is completely hydrolysed and then analysed by gas-liquid chromatography.

The chromatogram produced is shown in Fig. 8.2.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

Fig. 8.2

The number above each peak represents the area under the peak.

The area under each peak is proportional to the mass of the respective amino acid in the mixture.
parts.text: Calculate the percentage by mass of amino acid **A** in the original mixture.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The retention time for amino acid **D** is the longest.

Explain why **D** has a longer retention time than the **other** amino acids **A**, **B** and **C**.
